newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's foreign reserves drop to $15.179 bln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's foreign reserves drop to $15.179 bln.

text.p: Venezuela's foreign reserves dropped $5 million, or 0.03 percent, to $15.179 billion in the week to December 30, 1996, according to figures released by the Central Bank.
Reserves were down from $15.184 billion on December 23, the bank's weekly bulletin of indicators showed.
The Central Bank's annual year-end review published last week had seen foreign reserves ending 1996 at $15.133 billion.
Boosted by large capital inflows stemming from high international oil prices, Venezuela's foreign reserves rose over $5 billion last year.
This comfortably overshot the government's original target of $1.5 billion growth in 1996 as part of Venezuela's IMF-supported economic adjustment program launched mid-April.
Venezuela's reserves fell $1.784 billion, or 15.5 percent, in 1995 to end the year at $9.723 billion.
